background: ING Groep is the holding company of the Netherlands' largest bank, a digital-first retail and wholesale bank funded by deposits across the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany and other European markets, lending on mortgages and to corporates worldwide.
synthesis: The group is rated A on average across two of the three main agencies, the weaker of them at A-, both on a stable outlook, with the last move a one-notch upgrade by one of the three on 14 Apr 2016. Capital is on the weak side of EU and Nordic peers: CET1 of 13.0% and leverage of 4.3% are both in the bottom quarter against the peer medians, and both have fallen since 30 Jun 2024, CET1 by 1.0 points and leverage by 0.3 points. Liquidity is mixed, with LCR of 139% in the bottom quarter and NSFR of 128% above the peer median. The newest flagged item, on 2 Sep 2026, is an Australian capital add-on after the local unit overstated its liquidity, a control finding rather than a solvency one, set against a strong quarter reported over the summer.
